tasks.title: Resolve the stud-to-plate fastener
tasks.question: Which fastening schedule is documented for a stud end meeting the bottom or first top plate in the ICHL-015 reference wall?
tasks.scope: Use the 48 × 96-inch plain 2×6 frame. Identify the build and the OC16 or OC24 variant your evidence covers. The top-plate lap, adjoining panels and OSB each have separate fastening requirements.
completion: Identify a build record, drawing or reviewer who can tie a schedule to this joint and configuration.
For a proposed answer, cite the supporting record and record what it establishes about hardware, fasteners per joint, placement and installation. Mark any missing detail.
If applicability remains uncertain, name the competing sources and the specific detail a builder should confirm.

sources.title: OSE standard wall card
sources.excerpt: Screw studs through the bottom and first top plate (3-⅛″ T25) → frame.
sources.applicability: The card specifies a screw and the members it joins. It covers a panel with wrap, sheathing and insulation; it supplies no fastener count or positions for an ICHL-015 stud end.

sources.title: Earlier wall-family workflow
sources.excerpt: we use 3-1/4" ring shank nails as standard for the wood
sources.applicability: This configurable wall-family example also covers OSB. Its wood-fastener sentence gives no per-stud count, positions or link to a particular ICHL-015 build.

tasks.answer_evidence: Cite an independent build or reviewer record that identifies the applicable fastener for this joint and build.

tasks.title: Document the window-opening interface
tasks.question: For one identified window and wall configuration, what opening dimensions and reference faces should both contributors use, and what clearance or tolerance still needs confirmation?
tasks.scope: The released ICHL-015 OC16 and OC24 examples are plain walls. Use an opening-bearing configuration for this exercise. The existing exterior window panel below provides a candidate reference.
completion: Identify the wall and window configuration, with the drawing, build, or measurement that links them.
Describe which faces define the opening width and height, the sill datum, the units, and any documented clearance and tolerance.
If the records do not establish fit, capture the missing dimension or datum as a question for the next contributor.

sources.title: SEH 4 × 8 exterior window panel
sources.applicability: These three inch values describe the named OC16 model. It includes OSB and a window opening. Use independent evidence to identify the mating part, reference faces and allowable fit.

sources.title: ICHL-015 interface specifications
sources.excerpt: mating face, alignment reference, clearance, tolerance, connection requirement.
sources.applicability: The wall module lists Window Framing as an opening mate and calls for these interface fields. The list supplies no numerical clearance or tolerance for the window.

tasks.title: Find a quote for the wall lumber
tasks.question: What does a purchasing pack of 96-inch 2×6 framing lumber cost from one named supplier on a stated date?
tasks.scope: Use the OC16 plain-wall example and its lumber.2x6 purchasing line. The reference instance selects 96-inch stock. Record the stock length and purchasing unit exactly as the supplier describes them.
tasks.answer_evidence: Cite a dated supplier listing or quote for the specified lumber and purchasing unit.
completion: Identify the supplier, product link or shareable quote, date checked, stock length in inches, and USD price for one board or one pack.
State the number of boards in the quoted pack. Provide two distinct alternative product links or explain which alternatives you checked and why matching stock was unavailable.

If the supplier uses a different length or omits the pack size, submit the missing detail as a question. A lumber quote can settle one line while the hardware quantities and full wall total remain open.

tasks.title: Record one wall-width inspection
tasks.question: What width did someone actually measure across the outer stud faces of one identified plain wall frame?
tasks.scope: Use a physical ICHL-015 specimen. Identify its build and OC16 or OC24 spacing. The OC16 reference file supplies a 48-inch target and shows a pending inspection.
tasks.answer_evidence: Cite an independent inspection sheet, labelled measurement photo, or builder record that identifies the specimen and measured width.
completion: Name the specimen and spacing variant. Record the measured width in inches, instrument or method, measuring faces, and who took or reviewed the reading.
Cite the tolerance and its applicability to that build before proposing an acceptance result. Preserve an out-of-tolerance reading and its source.
If the specimen, measurement or tolerance is unavailable, identify exactly what someone needs to observe or confirm. A drawing dimension alone leaves the physical inspection pending.

tasks.title: Document the side joint between two walls
tasks.question: For one pair of adjacent ICHL-015 walls, how should the right face of one frame line up with the left face of the next?
tasks.scope: Identify two actual walls or a documented pair and their spacing variants. Work on a straight side-to-side joint between plain frames. Corners, internal stud-to-plate joints, openings and the roof use other details.
tasks.answer_evidence: Cite an independent assembly drawing, fit record or reviewer’s detail that identifies both mating walls.
completion: Name each module or specimen and its mating face. Identify a shared alignment reference and the source drawing, build or reviewer that connects those faces.
Record the required clearance and tolerance with units and their source, plus the documented connection requirement. Mark each unknown explicitly.
Describe whether the record specifies a designed fit or reports an actual fit check. If only the nominal profiles are known, ask for a reviewed interface detail or a specimen-specific fit record.
